A passenger jet with 239 people vanished into thin air—and flew in total silence for six hours.
In 2014, Malaysia Airlines flight 370 took off from Kuala Lumpur into the midnight sky.
At the border of airspace, its transponder was manually switched off, cutting every radar signal.
Military radar tracked it making a sharp, deliberate U-turn back across the peninsula, with zero distress calls.
Then, an overhead satellite picked up seven silent electronic pings, leading deep into the freezing southern Indian Ocean.
Ships searched over 120,000 square kilometers of deep abyss in the most expensive hunt in history.
Years later, scattered wings washed ashore thousands of miles away in Africa, but the plane was never found.
